headline: Strong Saturday storm brings wind and rain; drier, near-normal weather follows next week.
summary: Western Washington is in the path of a series of storms coming off the Pacific. The main event is a stronger system on Saturday, with Saturday night expected to be the peak. The strongest winds should hit the coast and the San Juans, and periods of heavy rain are expected on the coast and in the Olympics. The Skokomish River is at risk of flooding, though forecasters say river flooding is not expected on other rivers at this time. By midweek, the storm track is expected to shift south of the region, bringing drier, cooler weather. A blocking pattern over the West is expected to keep things dry later in the week. Next week should be calmer, with scattered showers early on and temperatures near average. Forecasters are fairly confident about the weekend storm and the drier pattern, but less certain about the flooding.
changes: Compared with the morning update, the afternoon discussion firmed up the Saturday wind threat, with a Wind Advisory now covering the coast and the San Juans. It also added a blocking pattern to explain the dry late-week outlook.
